sections.html:
Which notice a landlord sends turns on why the tenancy is ending. A court will not grant an order of possession unless the landlord offers a proper termination notice and the judge admits it as evidence. Unpaid rent, a lease breach, and the end of a month-to-month tenancy each run on a different clock.

SituationNotice periodCode section
Unpaid rent14 days after written notice to pay55.1-1245(F)
Breach that can be fixedLease ends no sooner than 30 days after receipt if not fixed in 21 days55.1-1245(A)
Breach that cannot be fixedNo sooner than 30 days after receipt55.1-1245(C)
Criminal or willful act threatening health or safetyImmediate termination and a possession case55.1-1245(C)
Week-to-week tenancy7 days before the next rent due date55.1-1253(A)
Month-to-month tenancy30 days before the next rent due date, unless the lease says otherwise55.1-1253(A)

The landlord serves a written notice stating that rent is unpaid and that the lease ends unless the tenant pays within 14 days. Termination is allowed only if the tenant still has not paid when those 14 days run out.

The same 14-day route covers a bounced rent check or an electronic payment rejected for insufficient funds. In that situation the notice must say the rent has to be paid by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or a completed electronic funds transfer.

A rule change takes effect July 1, 2027. After that date a landlord who owns more than four rental units in Virginia, or holds more than a 10 percent interest in more than four, must first send a notice with the exact amount owed when the debt is no more than one month's rent plus contracted late charges. That notice has to offer a payment plan lasting the lesser of six months or the time left on the lease, and the landlord only has to make the offer once during the lease term.

  • Until July 1, 2027: a 14-day written notice, then a possession case under 55.1-1251.
  • From July 1, 2027: larger landlords add the exact-amount notice and the payment plan offer.
  • Late fees stop accruing on the covered debt while the tenant keeps up with the plan.

sections.h2: When a tenant breaks other lease terms
sections.html:
If the tenant can correct the problem, the landlord serves a notice naming the acts or omissions. It says the lease will end on a date at least 30 days after receipt unless the breach is remedied within 21 days. A tenant who fixes it before that date keeps the lease.

A repeat of a similar breach after the first was fixed lets the landlord serve a notice that refers back to the earlier breach. That notice ends the lease no sooner than 30 days after receipt, and no new cure period applies.

Serious conduct gets harsher treatment. Illegal drug activity involving a controlled substance, or another criminal or willful act that threatens health or safety, is an immediate nonremediable violation. That holds even when the tenant did not personally act, because a tenant is presumed to know about activity by an authorized occupant, guest, or invitee unless the tenant proves otherwise. The landlord need not wait for a criminal conviction. The court sets an initial hearing within 15 calendar days of service, and a later hearing or trial follows within 30 calendar days of service.

Once the notice period passes, the landlord files a sworn statement and obtains a summons for unlawful detainer from a magistrate, clerk, or judge of the general district court. In residential cases the first hearing should land within 21 days of filing, or 30 days at the latest if the court cannot hear it sooner.

The tenant must be served at least 10 days before the return day. The landlord can ask for all rent due as of the hearing date and may amend the figure if more comes due before the case ends. Rent is not prorated to the hearing date when the lease makes rent due on the first for the whole month and the landlord asks for the full month.

Steps in order:

  • File the sworn statement and get the summons.
  • Serve the tenant at least 10 days before the return date.
  • Attend the first hearing, held within 21 days of filing or 30 at the latest.
  • Present the termination notice and the lease. Photocopies are allowed with an affidavit.

If the judge grants possession, the writ of eviction can be ordered to issue right away when the landlord asks. The summons also warns that an employer may not punish a tenant for missing work to come to court.

sections.h2: Appeal time and the sheriff's writ
sections.html:
A tenant has 10 days to appeal a general district court judgment to the circuit court, and the sheriff cannot carry out an eviction before that period ends. Appealing takes a bond and payment of the writ tax within the same 10 days, though an indigent defendant does not post an appeal bond.

After a writ issues, the sheriff must give notice of intent to execute at least 72 hours ahead, with the date and time. The writ has to be issued within 180 days of the possession judgment and can be returned within 30 days. A writ not executed in 30 days is vacated by operation of law.

If the landlord signs a new written rental agreement with the tenant after the possession judgment, no writ issues.

sections.h2: Occupants with no lease and former owners after foreclosure
sections.html:
These two situations follow their own rules. Suppose the owner of a single-family home proves that no rental agreement ever existed, that the occupant has no permission to be there, and that written notice to vacate went out at least 72 hours before filing. The court then sets an emergency hearing within 14 days of filing, or 30 days at the outside.

A former owner still living in a single-family home on the day of a foreclosure sale becomes a tenant at sufferance. The new owner ends that tenancy with written notice delivered at least three days before the effective date, then files for unlawful detainer. The former owner owes fair market rent from the sale date, plus damages, attorney fees, and court costs.

Squatting and adverse possession are a separate legal question, covered on another page of this site.

Besides possession, a landlord can seek unpaid rent, actual damages, reasonable attorney fees, and service costs. Code 55.1-1251 bars a post-possession judgment for accelerated rent through the end of the term, and the landlord has a duty to mitigate damages.

The court may enter one judgment for money and possession without crediting the security deposit. After the tenant moves out, the deposit is credited under the Virginia deposit rules.

A tenant who stays past the end of the lease without consent can be sued for possession and actual damages. The lease may set liquidated damages of up to 150 percent of the daily rent for each day the tenant remains. For public or HUD-regulated housing the cap is the plain daily rent.

sections.h2: Selling a rental during an eviction
sections.html:
A landlord who wants to sell still has to end or honor the tenancy through the steps above. A notice alone does not empty the house, and the sheriff, not the landlord, carries out a writ. A buyer will usually ask where the tenant stands, so a clear paper trail speeds things up.

Have these ready before you talk to any buyer:

  • Your notice dates and the case number, if there is one.
  • Whether the tenant is paying and how much is behind.
  • Photos of the property, the lease, rent receipts, and any damage records.

We buy houses as-is, including rentals with a tenant in place and vacant houses that need work. Send us the facts and we will tell you what we can offer. For questions about whether a particular notice is valid, talk to a Virginia landlord-tenant attorney or a legal aid office.

faqs.q: How many days of notice does a landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: Written notice with a 14-day wait for payment comes before termination and a possession case, under Code 55.1-1245(F).

faqs.q: How much notice ends a month-to-month tenancy?
faqs.a: Either side gives written notice at least 30 days before the next rent due date, unless the rental agreement sets another period (Code 55.1-1253).

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict right away for criminal activity?
faqs.a: In limited cases, yes. A criminal or willful act threatening health or safety, including illegal drug activity, allows immediate termination and a possession case. No conviction is needed first.

faqs.q: How long does a tenant have to appeal an eviction judgment?
faqs.a: Ten days to appeal to the circuit court. The sheriff cannot evict while that period runs (Code 8.01-129).

faqs.q: How long is a writ of eviction good for?
faqs.a: It must issue within 180 days of the possession judgment and be executed within 30 days of issuance, or it is vacated (Code 8.01-471).
